name: Data Analyzer: Text equality check ignores upper/lower case
objective: Proves that an 'equals' condition on text matches regardless of capital letters.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Test the condition 'column g equals male' on a 3-row table.
steps.expected: Result per row is: match, no match, match.

name: Data Analyzer: 'Is one of' condition matches any listed value
objective: Proves that an 'is one of' condition matches each value in the list, ignoring case.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Test 'g is one of male, m, 1' on a 4-row table.
steps.expected: Result per row is: match, match, no match, match.

name: Data Analyzer: Numeric 'greater than or equal' check handles blanks and text
objective: Proves that an 'age is at least 18' condition works on numbers and treats blank and non-numeric entries as not matching rather than failing.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Test 'age is at least 18' on a 5-row table.
steps.expected: Result per row is: no, yes, yes, no, no.

name: Data Analyzer: A condition on a missing column matches nothing
objective: Proves that a condition naming a column that does not exist is quietly false for every row and does not crash.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Test 'nonexistent equals x' on a table that has only column a.
steps.expected: Result is no match for both rows.

name: Data Analyzer: Blank and not-blank checks treat empty and space-only cells as blank
objective: Proves that empty, missing and whitespace-only cells all count as blank, and the opposite check mirrors it.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Run the 'is blank' and 'is not blank' conditions on a 4-row column.
steps.data: Values: 'x', missing, three spaces, empty text
steps.expected: Is-blank gives: no, yes, yes, yes. Is-not-blank gives: yes, no, no, no.

name: Data Analyzer: 'Contains text' check is case-insensitive and ignores missing cells
objective: Proves that a 'contains' condition finds a word inside longer text regardless of case, and does not match missing cells.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Test 'notes contains diabet' on a 3-row column.
steps.expected: Result per row is: match, no match, no match.

name: Data Analyzer: AND, OR and NOT combine conditions correctly
objective: Proves that conditions can be combined with AND, OR and NOT and give the expected row-by-row answers.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Test 'g equals m AND age at least 18' on 3 rows.
steps.expected: Result: yes, no, no.

steps.action: Test 'g equals f OR age at least 18', then 'NOT g equals m'.
steps.expected: OR gives yes, no, yes. NOT gives no, no, yes.

name: Data Analyzer: Fixed true/false conditions apply to every row
objective: Proves that a constant 'always true' or 'always false' condition gives the same answer for all rows.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Evaluate constant True and constant False on a 3-row table.
steps.expected: True gives yes for all three rows; False gives no for all three.

name: Data Analyzer: An unknown comparison type is rejected
objective: Proves that building a condition with a comparison type that does not exist raises an error immediately, rather than being accepted.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Create a condition using the made-up comparison type 'totally_bogus'.
steps.expected: A ValueError (invalid value error) is raised.

name: Data Analyzer: A condition survives being saved and reloaded
objective: Proves that a nested condition converted to stored form and back behaves identically.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Convert a nested AND/OR/NOT condition to stored form, rebuild it, and evaluate both on the same table.
steps.data: 2-row table with gender, age, x columns
steps.expected: The rebuilt condition gives exactly the same results as the original.

name: Data Analyzer: An old code-like text condition is turned into 'always false', never run
objective: Security check: old saved data may hold a condition written as program text (here a command that would delete files). Proves it is converted to a harmless always-false condition and not executed.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Rebuild a condition from the text "os.system('rm -rf /')".
steps.expected: The result is a constant condition whose value is False. Nothing is executed.

name: Data Analyzer: Unrecognised or empty stored conditions become 'always false'
objective: Proves that a stored condition of unknown type, or an empty one, becomes a constant condition instead of failing.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Rebuild conditions from an unknown-type record and from nothing.
steps.expected: Both results are constant conditions. (The test checks the kind, and does not check the value for these two.)

name: Data Analyzer: A conditional rule can be created with its details
objective: Proves that a rule built from made-up details keeps its identifier and holds a structured condition.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Create the sample rule (skip pregnancy questions for male subjects).
steps.expected: The rule id is 'pregnancy_gender_check' and its condition is a structured condition object.

name: Data Analyzer: A rule given a code-like text condition gets an inert condition
objective: Security check: if a rule is created with a condition written as program text (an attempt to run a command), the text is not executed and is replaced by 'always false'.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Create a rule whose condition is the text "__import__('os').system('boom')".
steps.expected: The rule's condition is a constant whose value is False.

name: Data Analyzer: A rule survives being saved and reloaded
objective: Proves that a rule converted to stored form and rebuilt keeps its identifier and condition.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Convert the sample rule to stored form and rebuild it.
steps.expected: The rebuilt rule has the same rule id and the same condition.

name: Data Analyzer: A condition can be printed in readable form
objective: Proves that showing a condition as text works and mentions the column it checks.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Convert the sample rule's condition to text.
steps.expected: The text contains the word 'gender' (any case).

name: Data Analyzer: A rule violation record can be converted to a plain record
objective: Proves that a violation (a data row that broke a rule) can be turned into a plain record. Only two of its values are checked.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Convert a made-up violation to a plain record.
steps.data: Rule id r, row 0, field f, value x, severity error
steps.expected: The record has rule_id 'r' and row_index 0. Other values are not checked.

name: Data Analyzer: REDCap condition text 'column equals value' is understood
objective: Proves that a simple REDCap branching expression is turned into a working check.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Parse "[gender]='2'" and apply it to 2 rows.
steps.expected: Result: yes, no.

name: Data Analyzer: REDCap 'and' conditions are understood
objective: Proves that an expression joining two checks with 'and' needs both to hold.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Parse "[diabetes]='1' and [age] >= 18" and apply it to 3 rows.
steps.expected: Result: yes, no, no.

name: Data Analyzer: REDCap 'or' conditions are understood
objective: Proves that an expression joining two checks with 'or' needs either to hold.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Parse "[status]='complete' or [status]='partial'" and apply it to 3 rows.
steps.expected: Result: yes, yes, no.

name: Data Analyzer: Brackets in REDCap conditions are respected
objective: Proves that grouping with parentheses changes evaluation order correctly.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Parse "([a]='1' or [a]='2') and [b]>=5" and apply it to 3 rows.
steps.expected: Result: yes, no, no.

name: Data Analyzer: Text that is not valid REDCap logic becomes 'always false'
objective: Security check: text that is program code rather than REDCap logic (a call to read a file) is not run and becomes an always-false condition.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Parse the text "pd.read_pickle('/tmp/evil.pkl')".
steps.expected: The result is a constant condition whose value is False.

name: Data Analyzer: An empty REDCap condition gives a fixed condition
objective: Proves that empty text does not cause an error and yields a constant condition. The value itself is not checked.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Parse empty text.
steps.expected: The result is a constant condition.

name: Data Analyzer: No fields means no rules
objective: Proves that extracting rules from an empty list of fields returns an empty list.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Extract rules from an empty field list.
steps.expected: The result is an empty list.

name: Data Analyzer: A REDCap 'show only if' becomes a 'must be blank otherwise' rule
objective: Proves that a field shown only when gender is 2 produces a rule affecting that field, which fires for rows where gender is not 2.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Build a rule for field 'pregnant' from "[gender]='2'".
steps.expected: A rule is returned and its affected field list is ['pregnant'].

steps.action: Apply the rule's condition to a male row that still has an answer.
steps.expected: The condition is true, meaning the rule applies to that row.

name: Data Analyzer: Rules are extracted for each field that has branching logic
objective: Proves that extracting rules from a made-up REDCap dictionary produces rules for the fields 'pregnant' and 'weeks_pregnant'.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Extract rules from four made-up fields, two of which have branching logic.
steps.expected: At least one rule identifier mentions 'pregnant' and at least one mentions 'weeks_pregnant'. (Both words also match the weeks_pregnant rule, so the first check is lenient.)

name: Data Analyzer: Plain-English 'If male, skip this field' becomes a must-be-blank rule
objective: Proves that a simple business-rule sentence is converted to a rule that expects the field to be blank for males.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Build a rule from the sentence 'If male, skip this field' for field 'pregnant'.
steps.expected: A rule is returned and its action is 'must_be_blank'.

steps.action: Apply its condition to two rows.
steps.expected: Result: yes, no.

name: Data Analyzer: Plain-English 'Required for female subjects' becomes a must-be-filled rule
objective: Proves that a 'required for' sentence is converted to a rule that expects the field to be filled.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Build a rule from 'Required for female subjects' for field 'preg_test'.
steps.expected: A rule is returned and its action is 'must_be_filled'.

name: Data Analyzer: A FHIR 'enable when' condition becomes a rule
objective: Proves that a FHIR questionnaire condition (enabled when gender is female) is converted into a rule that does not fire for female rows.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Build a rule for field 'pregnant' from a made-up FHIR condition and apply it to a female row.
steps.data: enableWhen: question gender, operator =, code female; row gender = female, pregnant = 1
steps.expected: A rule is returned and its condition gives False (no violation) for the female row.

name: Data Analyzer: Rules suggested by the AI in a dictionary are converted
objective: Proves that a rule written as 'gender is male' (as an AI model might output it) is turned into a working check. No AI is called; the rule is part of the test input.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Extract rules from a field that carries one pre-written rule.
steps.data: Field pregnant, rule 'gender is male' must be blank
steps.expected: Exactly one rule is produced, and its condition gives yes for male and no for female.

name: Data Analyzer: Plain-English conditions are understood in three forms
objective: Proves that 'age >= 18', 'status is not active' and 'notes contains diabetes' each become correct checks.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Convert three plain-English conditions and apply each to a 2-row table.
steps.expected: Results: age check yes,no; status check no,yes; notes check yes,no.

name: Data Analyzer: Validating with no rules finds no problems
objective: Proves that giving the validator no rules returns no violations.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Validate a 1-row table with an empty rule list.
steps.expected: The result is an empty list.

name: Data Analyzer: Validating an empty table finds no problems
objective: Proves that an empty data table does not cause an error and returns no violations.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Validate an empty table against two sample rules.
steps.expected: The result is an empty list.

name: Data Analyzer: Correct data produces no violations
objective: Proves that data that follows the rules is not flagged.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Validate a 3-row table that follows both sample rules (males blank on pregnancy, adults have consent).
steps.expected: The result is an empty list.

name: Data Analyzer: Data that breaks a 'must be blank' rule is flagged
objective: Proves that every offending cell is reported as a violation of error severity.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Validate two male rows that wrongly have pregnancy answers.
steps.data: Row 0: pregnant Yes, weeks 12; row 1: pregnant No
steps.expected: Exactly 3 violations are reported (2 for row 0, 1 for row 1), all with severity 'error'.

name: Data Analyzer: A missing required answer is flagged
objective: Proves that an 'adults need consent' rule flags an adult with a blank consent and ignores a child.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Validate two rows against the rule 'age at least 18 requires consent'.
steps.data: age 25 and 10; consent blank for both
steps.expected: Exactly one violation is reported, for row 0.

name: Data Analyzer: Validation continues past a problem rule (weakly tested)
objective: Intended to prove one faulty rule does not stop others. As written only a single valid rule is supplied (no faulty rule), so it really proves a normal rule reports at least one violation.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Validate two male rows against one valid 'must be blank' rule.
steps.data: Rule: gender equals Male, pregnant must be blank
steps.expected: At least one violation is reported.

name: Data Analyzer: Malicious dictionary logic that would run a command is not executed
objective: Security check: a data dictionary whose 'branching logic' is an attack (loading a booby-trapped file that would create a marker file) must not run.
precondition: Offline test harness; a temporary folder holds a booby-trapped file that would create a marker file named PWNED.txt if loaded.

steps.action: Extract rules from a dictionary field whose branching logic loads the booby-trapped file, then validate a small table.
steps.expected: No error; extraction and validation complete.

steps.action: Check for the marker file and the shape of the resulting rule.
steps.expected: The marker file does not exist. The rule's condition is a NOT around a constant False, so it is inert.

name: Data Analyzer: AI-style rule text containing a system command is not executed
objective: Security check: a rule whose condition text tries to run an operating-system command must not run it.
precondition: Offline test harness; temporary folder; the command would create a marker file named PWNED2.txt.

steps.action: Extract rules from a field whose rule text is a command, then validate a table.
steps.expected: The marker file does not exist (the command was not run).

name: Data Analyzer: The logic engine's source contains no code-execution calls
objective: Security check: the source file of the logic engine must not contain the text 'exec(' or 'eval('. A plain text search, so it also would flag a comment that contains those words.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Read the logic engine source file and search it.
steps.expected: The text 'exec(' is absent and the text 'eval(' is absent.

name: Data Analyzer: One badly formed dictionary field does not stop the others
objective: Proves that fields with unusable logic (a number, a list) do not prevent rules being extracted for the good fields.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Extract rules from four fields, two with valid logic and two with a number or list as logic.
steps.data: legit_a [gender]='2'; evil 123; legit_b [age]>=18; also_bad a list
steps.expected: Rules exist for legit_a and for legit_b. No error is raised.

name: Data Analyzer: Entries that are not proper fields are skipped
objective: Proves that stray items in a field list (text, empty) are ignored and the valid field still gives a rule.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Extract rules from a list containing text, nothing, and one valid field.
steps.data: 'not a dict', None, field 'ok' with logic [g]='1'
steps.expected: A rule whose identifier mentions 'ok' is produced; no error is raised.

name: Data Analyzer: A saved rule holding file-reading code is made inert
objective: Security check: a stored rule whose condition is program text (reading a system password file) is rebuilt as an always-false condition and not run.
precondition: Offline test harness; the conditional-logic checking component is used directly on small made-up tables. No network, no AI model.

steps.action: Rebuild a rule from stored form with condition text "open('/etc/passwd').read()".
steps.expected: The rule's condition is a constant whose value is False.
